aspects.says: jPOS CMF is also a complete message format based on ISO 8583:2003, whose cmf.xml packager unpacks field 4 as an ISOAmount carrying its currency.
basis: section:16.3 A Destination's Code Becomes a Cause, and Each Source's Table Answers It
aspects.reason: background on a packager the switch does not use; there is no decision a reader makes that a test could grade

aspects.says: A destination's response code is translated into a cause and each source's table turns the cause into its own code; passed through, a code from another format can make the reply unsendable.
basis: section:16.3 A Destination's Code Becomes a Cause, and Each Source's Table Answers It

aspects.says: A plain participant after QueryHost runs only while the transaction is prepared; with continuations off, a timeout aborts first and nothing reverses the silent purchase.
basis: section:16.4 A Code the Table Lacks Is Like Silence, and the Switch Reverses What It Sent

aspects.says: The destination receives a copy of the source's request; every answer to the source, approval, decline or 91 alike, is built from the unchanged request, so renumbering the request in place breaks every answer.
basis: section:16.1 The Destination Gets a Copy Numbered by the Switch, and Every Answer Starts From the Source's Request

aspects.says: The record is written before the request leaves, because the purchase that most needs a reversal is the one whose answer never came.
basis: section:16.2 A Source's Reversal Finds What the Destination Saw Only Through the Switch's Record

aspects.says: The record is taken, not read, so a repeated reversal goes upstream once, and it is kept without track data, PIN block or chip data.
basis: section:16.2 A Source's Reversal Finds What the Destination Saw Only Through the Switch's Record

aspects.says: A source's reversal names the source's original, which the destination never saw; the switch finds the upstream message through its own record and reverses that, so field 90 names what the destination received.
basis: section:16.2 A Source's Reversal Finds What the Destination Saw Only Through the Switch's Record

aspects.says: On each upstream link the switch is the sender, so the copy carries a STAN from one sequence per destination link and the switch's own identifiers.
basis: section:16.1 The Destination Gets a Copy Numbered by the Switch, and Every Answer Starts From the Source's Request

aspects.says: A code the destination's table lacks leaves the outcome unknown, like silence, so the switch reverses what it sent, once, and answers 96 or 91 rather than a decline.
basis: section:16.4 A Code the Table Lacks Is Like Silence, and the Switch Reverses What It Sent
